title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Understanding of Article 56 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases
keywords_en: labor contract; bankruptcy; economic compensation; court's adjudication of enterprise bankruptcy cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Reply on the Understanding of Article 56 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases

Fa Han [2003] No. 46

Ministry of Labor and Social Security:

We have received your letter of December 15, 2002, seeking advice on issues arising from the implementation of Article 56 of our "Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases" (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions"). Upon study, we reply as follows:

1. Article 56 of the Provisions is not applicable to enterprise bankruptcy cases that are subject to national planned adjustment. For such enterprise bankruptcy cases, the relevant provisions of the State Council's Notice on Issues concerning the Trial Implementation of Bankruptcy of State-owned Enterprises in Certain Cities (Guofa [1994] No. 59) and the Supplementary Notice on Issues concerning the Trial Implementation of Merger and Bankruptcy of State-owned Enterprises and Reemployment of Workers in Certain Cities (Guofa [1997] No. 10) shall apply. After the payment of resettlement fees and economic compensation to the workers of the bankrupt enterprise in accordance with the relevant provisions, no further compensation for the termination of labor contracts shall be paid.

2. The meaning of "in accordance with the law or in accordance with the labor contract" in Article 56 of the Provisions is as follows: First, the amount of compensation shall be determined in accordance with the terms of the labor contract; if the labor contract has no such terms, compensation shall be determined in accordance with laws, regulations, and with reference to relevant provisions of departmental rules. Second, if the compensation amount agreed in the labor contract or determined pursuant to relevant provisions is excessively high or low, the liquidation team may adjust it in accordance with relevant provisions. The standard for adjustment shall be based on the average monthly wage of the worker over the twelve-month period under normal operating conditions of the bankrupt enterprise. Third, after adjustment by the liquidation team, if the enterprise's trade union or individual workers believe that the compensation is still too low, they may apply to the people's court accepting the bankruptcy case for a change; if the creditors' meeting has objections to the compensation for workers determined by the liquidation team, the procedure provided in Article 44 of the Provisions shall be followed.

This reply is given.

September 9, 2003
